label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: none

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. I’ve been at this 26 years and I still walked in there thinking, well, that’s a new one.

The power supply was three orange extension cords daisy chained out the basement window, across the yard and under the deck. One splice was wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. Apparently if the Red Green Show had an electrical department.

Opened up a box and found a mouse nest. Mice were fine, completely unbothered. They may have been the only ones in there with any sense.

The shed outlet was hooked up with speaker wire. The ceiling fan box was hanging on by one drywall screw and a prayer. There was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on it, which is about as effective as putting a Steelers sticker on my truck and expecting it to play linebacker.

And then I opened the panel. Written inside the door in Sharpie:

SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

The wife was standing there, looks at it and goes, “Who’s Ron?”

I don’t know! But Ron apparently wanted the shed left alone.

Now, I’m laughing because some of this was ridiculous, but I’m not putting the guy who did it on trial. He wasn’t evil. He was cheap and a little proud, and honestly that’s most of these jobs. Somebody figures it worked yesterday, so it must be fine. Then somebody else adds another cord or another outlet and pretty soon the whole thing is one bad day away from trouble.

There was also a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. That’s not a funny one. The breaker is supposed to protect the wire, and an oversized breaker can let that wire overheat before it trips. Stuff like this can start a fire in a shed, and the same kind of work can burn a house down.

We trenched it, ran proper cable, put it on a 20 amp GFCI breaker, installed real boxes and outlets, and got the fan on a proper brace. Fan’s running, nothing smells like burning, and the mice will have to find other accommodations.

I got paid in two pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which is a solid Saturday rate when it’s a buddy.

Seriously though: if you’ve got questionable wiring, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy who watched a YouTube video and says he can probably figure it out. Electricity doesn’t care how confident he sounds.
